# Local initial-binding scope patch

Upstream: spareval 0.2.7, Oxigraph commit `0e81a29d27575ab69e7f85ea9c7f1058b277fcd0`. `UPSTREAM-PROVENANCE.json` records the original Cargo crate and exact source-file identities. Both upstream licenses are included. The original crate version is retained; the workspace path dependency and source hash identify this local implementation.

Application substitutions are read from one evaluator context. Project gives child evaluation access to that context and returns only its explicit projected domain. Expression lookup may read an initial value without adding a binding to the row. Graph leaves reconstruct the initial context, matching the frozen RDFLib boundary. CONSTRUCT templates apply initial fallback after the algebra has evaluated, so it does not change MINUS domains. Empty substitution lists retain the original evaluator path. No alternate Dataset or string-based query rewriting is used.

The engineering adapter keeps typed parameter budgets, local-only query checks, result budgets and 8 MiB query stack. Reassignment and aggregate-target boundaries remain refused. The prior source-frozen behavior refused hidden DESCRIBE application parameters. This increment preserves the parser's target projection, captures its target slots before encoding any unused application parameters, and makes `DescribeIterator` enumerate only those target slots. Visible initial resources remain legitimate targets, and hidden values remain readable in WHERE. It uses the same evaluator and Dataset; it does not create a second Dataset, rewrite the input query or mask parameter values.

The original hidden-parameter DESCRIBE among the frozen 15 options cases is compared with its exact four `urn:part` triples. Separate original DESCRIBE observations preserve RDFLib 7.6 errors and output differences; current wildcard controls are not labelled successful original wildcard executions. An explicit parser/evaluator target metadata path supports profile2: modifier keys may include child projections, but `with_describe_target_variables` preserves only genuine target variables as resource slots. The adjacent spargebra parser provides the compatibility key `Distinct` before `Slice`, preserving original modifier-zero and nested-four observations. Neutral parser defaults remain intact. Precise baseline/upstream source and license identities are recorded in `DESCRIBE-PATCH-PROVENANCE.json`. Independent original outputs, all failed trials and current execution identities are retained separately. These finite checks do not establish complete DESCRIBE, SPARQL, Semantica or engineering qualification.

All local evaluator Rust and Cargo files, its upstream manifest and the frozen test inputs enter the existing compiled-source authority; the real ggen source map binds the same inputs. The complete original Semantica scope remains unchanged and incomplete. Software query parity does not authorize engineering adoption or a whole-code version switch.

A separate shared Count correction uses specialized expression/distinct wrappers so errors or unbound values skip one row, matching existing CountInternal. Valid values remain counted before/after errors; DISTINCT stores only valid exact terms. The general Expression failure policy for Sum/Avg/Min/Max stays unchanged. Independent W3C expectation0, historical RDFLib error-count3 and prior Rust unbound remain distinct. No DTO/profile/parser/context guard or Dataset change is introduced. COUNT-PATCH-PROVENANCE.json preserves upstream/previous source/license/oracle identities.

The nullable carrier foundation moves the existing InternalTuple into `src/tuple.rs` with separate local absence, RDF, explicit None and returned-error cells. Existing Project, ordinary joins, Union, DISTINCT, MINUS, hash keys, pattern assignment and SELECT decoding use that carrier. Equal-value join representation and initial-shadow origin remain as before. RDF-only variable consumers may fall back to initial RDF only for a missing local cell. The shared result decoder retains presence; its legacy adapter rejects non-RDF cells instead of discarding them. These internal changes do not enable a public nullable query profile. `NULLABLE-PATCH-PROVENANCE.json` identifies the carrier's finite source-derived controls and prior implementation.

The subsequent private expression lane adds typed raw/operand/error boundaries to the same compiler, sharing the six legacy arithmetic kernels. Only a bounded integer subset is qualified for implementation; unproven numeric cases fail explicitly. COUNT/SAMPLE, Group, Extend and FILTER consume complete cells and propagate fatal failures; DISTINCT COUNT retains the original two evaluations. Old RDF grouping hashes and public query modes remain unchanged. The lane is disabled by default, has no public enablement and refuses unported operators. `NULLABLE-EXPRESSION-PROVENANCE.json` and `docs/SEMANTIC-NULLABLE-EXPRESSIONS.md` distinguish source-derived expectations, active safety differences and remaining numeric, parser, context and wrapper obligations. These changes do not claim full RDFLib or Semantica parity.

The next private arithmetic-chain increment carries source-preserving nonempty sequences through the existing parser/planner into the same compiler. First and the complete raw tail are evaluated before numeric work; each source chain captures SPARQL failure once, while nested chains keep their own boundary. A bounded integral state reuses the same arithmetic kernels and admits integral Decimal children only with compiler arithmetic provenance. Fractional intermediates, external Decimal, unsupported range and negative Decimal zero remain explicit fatal capability limits. Default modes stay unchanged, whole-query optimization is bypassed by private receiving, and public `/5` remains absent. `NULLABLE-CHAIN-PROVENANCE.json` records this new source identity without modifying previous qualification or original observations.
